continuity_scope: Nickelodeon's original animated Avatar: The Last Airbender continuity only, limited to Book One: Water, Episodes 1–2 ("The Boy in the Iceberg" and "The Avatar Returns") and the associated official Paramount+ series/episode metadata. Comics, novels, The Legend of Korra, live-action film/television, games, and all later episodes are excluded.
work_or_witnesses: Avatar: The Last Airbender, S1 E1: The Boy in the Iceberg (The Avatar Returns Part 1), Paramount+ episode page
Avatar: The Last Airbender, S1 E2: The Avatar Returns (Part 2), official Paramount+ Season 1 episode guide
Official Paramount+ Avatar: The Last Airbender series page, limited to its high-level setting description
coverage_rule: Include every individually named dramatic character directly named in the two selected official episode descriptions: Aang, Katara, Sokka, and Prince Zuko. Nations, the Southern Water Tribe, elemental disciplines, the Avatar office, the iceberg, village, animals, places, spiritual concepts, institutions, and war/conquest context remain terms or omissions rather than character nodes.
omissions: All named or unnamed figures not directly named by the selected E1–E2 official descriptions are outside this deliberately narrow opening-witness pass.
Books One–Three material beyond E2, comics, novels, The Legend of Korra, live-action adaptations, games, and other franchise continuities are excluded.

The selected metadata does not establish the full history, causes, or consequences of the Fire Nation's conquest; no genocide, colonialism, real-world historical analogy, or ethnicity/cultural-inspiration equivalence is asserted.
No disability, spiritual-practice, gender, romance, violence detail, child-harm event, or real-world cultural claim is inferred where the selected metadata does not explicitly establish it.
uncertainties: The United States E1 metadata calls Aang a twelve-year-old boy without naming him in the E1 sentence; the official series/episode guide and E2 metadata identify Aang. His E1 identity is therefore recorded only at the level supported across these official metadata locators.
"Avatar" and bending are fictional source terms. This pass does not turn them into universal religious, ethnic, martial, or game-class equivalents.
The official overview describes a four-nation setting and Fire Nation conquest at series level; it is used only for bounded setting terminology, not to add later-story character claims.
evidence_basis: Official Paramount+ (Nickelodeon/Paramount) episode and series metadata only. No fan wiki, Wikipedia, transcript, recap, franchise database, or adaptation source is used.
